text:
riley: Heads-up: did an AWQ int4 pass on Eos9B (Gemma fork) and long-document QA dropped hard. Short Qs look OK.

anika: numbers and command?

riley: fp16 rougeL 43.7 / qa-f1 69.5. awq-int4 -> rougeL 35.9 / qa-f1 60.8. command: `python3 tools/convert_awq.py --model eos9b.fp16 --out eos9b.awq4 --bits 4 --group 64 --perchannel`

morgan: repeating tokens or weird unicode tokens? those often show tokenizer normalization issues.

riley: yes, saw runs like: `... the \u200c the the ...` in decoded text (U+200C = ZWNJ) and some casefolding differences. Long docs trigger it.

anika: could be rotary handshake + tokenizer normalizer mismatch. Any rotary warnings in logs?

riley: small drift logged: `rotary_layer_12: scale=0.9991 expected=1.0` and later some headwise phase skew on layer 8. convert assumed per-head rotary scaling. Upstream metadata says `rotary: fractional_shared` (they use a per-head fractional scale in export).

morgan: fractional_shared? that's new. Means the model stores a shared base scale and a per-head fractional tweak. Our converter doesn't understand that, it chooses per_head or shared, causing phase errors. If AWQ quant adds noise, those mismatches amplify on long contexts.

anika: also normalization: upstream tokenizer does NFKC normalizer + emoji folding, whereas our local tokenizer uses NFD. That explains ZWNJ/ZWJ artifacts after remap. Did you use tokenizer packaged in model archive or our canonical tokenizers repo?

riley: archive tokenizer. convert_awq.py computed `vocab_n = len(vocab)` then assumed identity mapping. with extra normalization differences, some multi-codepoint graphemes got new ids appended to the tail which shifted special token indices.

ci-bot: nightly-run/6530001234: baseline fp16=43.7 int4(awq,naive)=35.9.

morgan: Plan: 1) extend converter to understand fractional_shared rotary (apply shared base * (1 + per_head_delta)), 2) add `--tokenizer-path` and enforce tokenizer normalization step during conversion (force upstream normalizer), 3) add a token-id tail smoke test and a unicode-normalization unit test.

anika: I can prototype fractional_shared handler quickly. Need a tiny probe to detect fractional pattern: check if per_head params = shared * (1 + small_delta). If yes, treat as fractional_shared.

morgan: I'll add tokenizer-normalizer enforcement in tools and a unit test that runs normalization on a failing transcript. Also add a small end-to-end AWQ slice test to CI.

riley: quick local try: re-run convert with `--rotary-mode fractional_shared --tokenizer-path ./tokenizer.json --normalize NFKC` then awq -> intermediate rougeL 42.0 / qa-f1 67.5. Much closer.

devops-bot: artifact-upload: s3://redwood-models/eos9b/awq_fallback/6530001234/ uploaded.

ci-bot: draft-pr/3460 opened by morgan: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-tools/pull/3460 (AWQ fractional_shared rotary, tokenizer normalization arg, unicode-smoke tests).

anika: added a tiny probe script to detect fractional_shared and wrote notes for the onboarding checklist: "if rotary param isn't strictly per_head or shared, run fractional probe".

morgan: test results after PR merged: awq-int4 rougeL 42.3 / qa-f1 68.1. long-doc hallucination rate down ~53%.

riley: closing loop. leaving a note in the model-onboarding playbook to always include `--tokenizer-path` and a rotary-probe step for Gemma/Mistral forks. reopen if we see new regressions.

ci-bot: thread archived at 6530001570.
